title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics and parity fixes across python/typescript/go; bump to v1.107.0
author: Jordan Kim
description: Motivation: We maintain three language SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) and have drifted in auth handling, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics. This PR unifies middleware/transport layers so application code has consistent behavior across languages, fixes several parity bugs discovered during cross-language conformance tests, and bumps SDK versions to v1.107.0. Summary of changes: 1) Centralize auth token refresh and error handling: introduced a language-idiomatic AuthTransport/AuthMiddleware that standardizes token refresh on 401/403, exponential backoff for transient auth errors, and a single place to configure custom token providers. Backwards compatibility: old auth hooks are preserved via a thin adapter that emits a deprecation warning for one release. 2) Unify retry policy surface: added RetryPolicy type (max_retries, backoff_base_ms, backoff_factor, retry_on) and implemented it across all SDKs. Default policy matches server-side SLOs; transparent for most users. 3) Streaming ergonomics: standardize event-oriented streaming API (on_data/on_error/on_done) across SDKs while keeping existing iterator-based streaming as a compatibility layer. Improved cancellation semantics and ensured KV-cache-friendly early termination does not leak resources. 4) Parity fixes: fixed TypeScript streaming reconnect bug under slow networks; fixed Go client header encoding bug causing 0.0.0.0 host in some proxies; fixed Python async iterator to surface partial data frames correctly. 5) Version bumps and changelogs: all SDKs bumped to v1.107.0 with consolidated changelog entries. Testing and CI: ran unit and integration tests for all three SDKs, added conformance tests that cross-validate retry/backoff traces and streaming events. Checklist: - [x] design approved in ENG-2312 - [x] impl for Python - [x] impl for TypeScript - [x] impl for Go - [x] integration tests - [x] docs and changelogs updated - [x] version bumps committed Notes on rollout: this change is backward compatible for the vast majority of users; deprecation warnings will guide migration away from legacy auth hooks. In case of customers relying on custom low-level transports, a compatibility adapter is provided and documented.
